title: Let the About page's storage usage follow the disk
head: 8713691bb605
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Truncating the stamp misses values that fastfetch rounds up even on the same GiB unit
leads.consequence: At 1000 GiB capacity, changing used from 536870900000 to 536876900000 bytes changes fastfetch's rounded 500.00 GiB to 500.01 GiB, but both stamps remain /dev/sda1 50000. About can show the old figure indefinitely until another reason redraws. Round at the display's boundary, or compare formatted used values instead of integer division. The new test's assertion that any change smaller than a whole quantum cannot appear on screen is incorrect.

leads.summary: Capacity-based quantum ignores fastfetch's independent unit selection for used bytes
leads.consequence: On a 1000 GiB filesystem at 500 MiB used, a 1 MiB increase changes fastfetch's displayed used value to 501 MiB. The stamp uses a 0.01 GiB quantum inferred from capacity and stays 48 on both probes, so the visible row remains stale. Include both the used and total display resolutions when calculating a stamp or compare fastfetch-equivalent output.

leads.summary: The local-only/excluded probe cannot follow disk rows fastfetch can print
leads.consequence: Fastfetch always accepts root even if its filesystem is overlay or remote, and explicitly accepts sshfs mounts by default; df -l skips remote sources and -x overlay skips an overlay root. If such a source is the only displayed disk, storage_stamp is empty and storage_changed always returns false, so the new polling never updates the displayed figure. Make the probe follow the displayed mountpoints or explain/support a restricted set.

leads.summary: A filesystem source containing spaces is dropped as a malformed row
leads.consequence: GNU df prints the source column verbatim, not quoted or escaped; `read -r source size used` consumes the first space-separated token as source and the second as size. With `/dev/mapper/my device`, size becomes `device`, fails the numeric guard, and a single-device stamp is empty, so subsequent used-space changes never repaint. Parse the two numeric fields from the right, preserving the full source string.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; coreutils df.c print_table prints cell as-is; Opus self-check confirmed with stubbed df; published as optional note

leads.summary: A nonzero df with partial output still triggers a storage change
leads.consequence: The process substitution's exit status is discarded by the successful `while read` loop. When df prints any valid rows but returns nonzero for another inaccessible mount, `storage_stamp` succeeds with a partial stamp, and `storage_changed` treats this as real change, contrary to the comment's failed-probe promise. It can redraw spuriously whenever a mount alternates between readable and failing; separately capture and gate df's exit status.
leads.triage: dropped; partial df output only redraws when the readable set changes; minor

leads.summary: Polling all local mounts can block the About window's key handling on an unresponsive mount
leads.consequence: Even when that mount is not in fastfetch's visible disk list, coreutils df traverses the selected local mounts and stats the paths; no timeout protects its every-half-second invocation. If a local mounted filesystem stops answering statfs, content_changed blocks inside df before tick reads a key, so closing About by typing becomes unavailable until the mount recovers. Consider scoping the probe to visible filesystems and bounding its runtime; not reproduced with a hung mount.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus_hypothesis; not reproduced; reflected by narrowing the Verified bullet

leads.summary: Unrelated local mounts cause full redraws without changing a visible disk row
leads.consequence: An ext4 filesystem on /dev/loop0 or /boot is included by this df probe but not by default fastfetch (loop devices excluded, boot hidden). Writes above the quantum on those mounts call fastfetch and clear the window repeatedly, without any new value on the disk row. The test explicitly expects a change on another mount to redraw, but never checks that the mount is shown. Restrict watches to visible mounts; source-only check, not runtime reproduced.
leads.triage: dropped; watching all local filesystems is the PR's stated design

leads.summary: The issue's continued staleness after a genuine fresh reopen is not explained by this PR's premise
leads.consequence: If 'Open/check the About page again' in the issue means close and start a new window, fastfetch already calls statvfs anew, so a mere lack of in-window rerender cannot explain a value that fails to decrease on reopening. An existing window is instead focused on repeated launch, which would support the PR's premise. Clarify which case the reporter saw, then check df/statvfs before and after deletion (open handles or snapshots may retain blocks). The cause of the report remains unconfirmed.

leads.summary: The new tests still pass when the production df unit is wrong
leads.consequence: Every new df test stub emits bytes regardless of the options requested. In a disposable copy, changing only `df -l -B1` to `df -l -B1024` still passes all 39 test assertions, although the real df now returns block counts where the stamp assumes bytes and will miss storage changes. Assert `-B1 --output=source,size,used` through the stub or exercise a synthetic command that respects requested block size. This is a test-fidelity issue, lower priority than the observable bugs.
leads.triage: verified; test line 177 stub ignores args; Opus sandbox2 showed --output drop also passes; published with --output example

leads.summary: Open PR #10751 has a test-file conflict with this PR
leads.consequence: The two nonstacked PRs both insert assertions just after the existing 'render loop plays the sheen' case. A three-way merge with #10751's own common ancestor leaves a conflict in launch-about-test.sh at merged lines 330-351, even though the production launcher merged without markers. Merging both will require keeping both tests explicitly. The other PR currently reports MERGEABLE with the base branch, not necessarily with this PR; this combination was source-merged only, not test-run.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; kept in local report only

limits: Fastfetch source is upstream dev commit ffbf4ec7; the relevant disk detection, formatting and display files are byte-identical to upstream tag 2.69.0 (0c3b852b). The package list does not pin an Arch fastfetch release, and no host installed package was queried.
No actual hung mounts, real host df or fastfetch host disk data were probed. Browser/GitHub discussion was not read. Source-only H6/H7 are conditional.
Merged test of #10751 cannot run before resolving its conflict. Other related PR merge results are file-level only; no deployment tests performed.

flags.claim: Before this PR, content_changed only compared the grid and the logo mtime, and omarchy-launch-or-focus focuses an existing About window, so an open window never refreshed the disk row.
flags.why: The base loop re-runs fastfetch, and so refreshes the disk row, whenever the window is resized (WINCH flag or grid change) or the logo mtime changes. 'Never refreshed' should be 'only refreshed on a resize or rebrand' (the PR description says the same). content_changed also checks the WINCH resized flag, not only the grid and mtime. My final.md Summary has the same overstatement, which contradicts its own 'only then' bullet.

flags.claim: With -l, remote mounts are skipped before any statfs, so a stale network mount cannot block the poll.
flags.why: The first half is correct. The second is too absolute. gnulib counts a mount as remote only when its source contains ':', is '-hosts', or its type is on a fixed list (nfs*, cifs, smb*, ceph, afs, lustre and others; no fuse.* types). A network-backed FUSE mount whose source has no ':' is treated as local and is stat'd and statfs'd on every poll. s3fs is an example, from general knowledge: /proc/mounts shows its source as 's3fs'. My final.md listed FUSE as an untested hypothesis. This is source-only; nothing was run.

flags.claim: The df stub ignores its arguments, so changing -B1 to -B1024 in the launcher still passes the whole file. A stub that checks for -B1 would catch it.
A seeded comparison against fastfetch's formatting rules (mirrored from its source, 1,500 trials for each of 7 sizes from 32 GB to 4 TB) found no missed and no redundant redraws with the change.
flags.why: The numbers are right: 0 missed and 0 redundant across 10500 trials. The comparison, however, only models the printed used figure, not the percentage or the total. The mirror uses awk printf %.2f, which differs from fastfetch's yyjson round-half-up only on exact binary ties. Adding 'for the used figure' would keep the qualifier.

flags.claim: df prints the source column verbatim, so a source containing a space splits into a non-numeric size and that filesystem is skipped. Reading the two numeric fields from the right of the line avoids this.
flags.why: A space is printed as a space. df copies the device name into the cell, gnulib turns mountinfo's \040 back into a space, and replace_problematic_chars only replaces control characters (and invalid multibyte when stdout is a tty) with '?'. 'Verbatim' is slightly strong: control characters become '?', and UUID-suffixed symlink device names are canonicalized. Whichever of the two read fields ends up non-numeric, the row is skipped (verified with a stub: 'My Drive ...' dropped). Relevance is low: fastfetch only shows /dev/* block devices plus /, ZFS, fuse.sshfs and WSL drvfs, so a source with a space is rarely a row on screen. The fix by reading from the right is correct by reasoning but was not run.

flags.claim: On filesystems of 1 TiB or more with under 1 TiB used, the probe misses most changes the storage row shows, such as a 2 GB deletion.
flags.why: Supported by the property run (TiB sizes: 384/450, 251/301 and 135/161 visible changes missed) and by the derived estimate that a 2 GiB deletion is missed about 80 % of the time. Nit: the Outcome says '2 GB' while the body and reproducer say '2 GiB'. Both are mostly missed (about 80 % and 82 %, derived), but the units should agree.

flags.claim: With the suggested change ..., this case passes, as does the PR's test file adjusted for the new stamp format.
flags.why: The PR test needed three adjustments, not only the stamp format. Details (line 144) lists all three, so nothing is lost overall.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** On filesystems of 1 TiB or more with under 1 TiB used, the probe misses most changes the storage row shows, such as a 2 GiB deletion.

### The redraw step comes from the disk size, but fastfetch sizes the used figure by itself

fastfetch formats used and total separately, each in its own unit. A 2 TB drive with 500 GiB used prints `500.00 GiB / 1.82 TiB`, but `storage_quantum` takes TiB from the size, so the stamp only moves every ~10.24 GiB. **Impact:** deleting 2 GiB there (500.00 → 498.00 GiB) usually leaves the old figure on screen. The stamp also truncates hundredths that fastfetch rounds, so the `+10737417` test case (500.00 → 500.01 GiB) is asserted not to redraw.

**Suggested change:** stamp the used bytes in their own unit, rounded to the nearest hundredth (`storage_figure` under Details), and flip the `+10737417` case.

<details><summary>Reproducer: 2 TB drive (fails at 8713691)</summary>

# Reproducer: the redraw step is taken from the filesystem size, not the used figure

Reviewed head: `8713691bb60593f17490ed7af382ac825123bdb2`.

fastfetch formats the used and total figures of the disk row separately, each in the unit that suits its own value (`src/modules/disk/disk.c` calls `ffSizeAppendNum` once for `bytesUsed` and once for `bytesTotal`; `src/common/impl/size.c` picks the unit from the value it is given). On a filesystem of 1 TiB or more with less than 1 TiB used, the total prints in TiB but the used figure prints in GiB with two decimals. `storage_quantum` derives the step from the size, so the probe only notices a change of about 10.24 GiB (10995116277 bytes).

## Test case

Add this to `test/shell.d/launch-about-test.sh`, after the PR's storage cases (after the `resized=false` that follows "a resize landing during the check redraws") and before the `# The grid costs a process ...` block:

```bash
# fastfetch picks the unit for each figure on its own. A 2 TB drive's total is
# drawn in TiB, but 500 GiB used on it is drawn in GiB, to two decimals of a GiB,
# so deleting 2 GiB moves the row from 500.00 GiB to 498.00 GiB.
df_output="Filesystem 1B-blocks Used
/dev/nvme0n1p2 1999844147200 536870912000"
storage_at_render=$(storage_stamp)
df_output="Filesystem 1B-blocks Used
/dev/nvme0n1p2 1999844147200 $(( 536870912000 - 2147483648 ))"
if content_changed; then
  pass "deleting 2 GiB on a 2 TB drive redraws"
else
  fail "deleting 2 GiB on a 2 TB drive redraws" "stamp before: $storage_at_render, after: $(storage_stamp)"
fi
```

Run: `bash test/shell.d/launch-about-test.sh`

## Actual output at the reviewed head (last lines)

```
ok - the probe leaves the memory filesystems out
ok - a resized window redraws whatever the storage says
ok - a rebranded logo redraws whatever the storage says
ok - a resize landing during the check redraws
stamp before: /dev/nvme0n1p2 48, after: /dev/nvme0n1p2 48
not ok - deleting 2 GiB on a 2 TB drive redraws
```

Exit status 1.

## What fastfetch prints for these values

Computed with a mirror of fastfetch's `appendNum` (IEC prefixes, two decimals, the unit chosen from the value itself), not by running fastfetch:

```
536870912000 bytes prints as 500.00 GiB
534723428352 bytes prints as 498.00 GiB
1999844147200 bytes prints as 1.82 TiB
```

So the row goes from `500.00 GiB / 1.82 TiB` to `498.00 GiB / 1.82 TiB`, and the window keeps showing `500.00 GiB`.

With the suggested change (unit from the used bytes, rounded to nearest), this case passes, as does the PR's test file adjusted for the new stamp format.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: rounding (fails at 8713691)</summary>

# Reproducer: the stamp cuts off hundredths that fastfetch rounds

Reviewed head: `8713691bb60593f17490ed7af382ac825123bdb2`.

`storage_stamp` prints `used / quantum` with integer division, which cuts the figure off at the hundredth. fastfetch rounds it to the nearest hundredth (`ffStrbufAppendDouble` with a fixed precision of 2, which rounds half up). A change of less than one step can therefore move the printed figure without moving the stamp. The PR's own case "a change short of a whole quantum leaves the render alone" (`df_used + 10737417`) is such a change: fastfetch prints it as 500.01 GiB against 500.00 GiB at render time.

## Test case

Add this to `test/shell.d/launch-about-test.sh` after the PR's storage cases, before the `# The grid costs a process ...` block:

```bash
# fastfetch rounds the two decimals rather than cutting them off, so a change of
# less than one hundredth can still move the figure it prints: 536870900000 bytes
# prints as 500.00 GiB and 536881637417 bytes as 500.01 GiB.
df_output="Filesystem 1B-blocks Used
/dev/sda1 1073741824000 536870900000"
storage_at_render=$(storage_stamp)
df_output="Filesystem 1B-blocks Used
/dev/sda1 1073741824000 536881637417"
if content_changed; then
  pass "a change that moves the printed hundredth redraws"
else
  fail "a change that moves the printed hundredth redraws" "stamp before: $storage_at_render, after: $(storage_stamp)"
fi
```

Run: `bash test/shell.d/launch-about-test.sh`

## Actual output at the reviewed head (last lines)

```
ok - the probe leaves the memory filesystems out
ok - a resized window redraws whatever the storage says
ok - a rebranded logo redraws whatever the storage says
ok - a resize landing during the check redraws
stamp before: /dev/sda1 50000, after: /dev/sda1 50000
not ok - a change that moves the printed hundredth redraws
```

Exit status 1.

## What fastfetch prints for these values

Computed with a mirror of fastfetch's `appendNum` (IEC prefixes, two decimals), not by running fastfetch:

```
536870900000 bytes prints as 500.00 GiB
536881637417 bytes prints as 500.01 GiB
```

The effect is small (the window can lag by 0.01 of the unit until the next step), but the PR's test pins the wrong expectation for this exact value.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Suggested replacement for `storage_quantum`, used as `printf '%s %s\n' "$source" "$(storage_figure "$used")"` in `storage_stamp` (the size is then only validated):

```bash
# The used figure as fastfetch prints it: the unit comes from the used bytes,
# not the filesystem size, and the hundredths are rounded, not cut off.
storage_figure() {
  local bytes="$1" unit=1 scale=$(( 10 ** STORAGE_DECIMALS ))

  while (( bytes / unit >= 1024 && unit < 1125899906842624 )); do
    unit=$(( unit * 1024 ))
  done

  printf '%d %d\n' "$unit" "$(( bytes / unit * scale + (bytes % unit * scale + unit / 2) / unit ))"
}
```

In a sandbox copy with this change, both reproducers pass, and the PR's test file passes after three adjustments: the header case expects `/dev/sda1 1073741824 50000`, the `+10737417` case expects a redraw, and the `storage_quantum` loop is removed. A seeded comparison against fastfetch's formatting rules (mirrored from its source, 1,500 trials for each of 7 sizes from 32 GB to 4 TB) found no missed and no redundant redraws for the used figure with the change.

**Verified**
- Before this PR the window only re-ran fastfetch on a resize or a logo change, and `omarchy-launch-or-focus` focuses an existing About window, so an open window otherwise kept its first disk figure.
- `df` Used and fastfetch's used bytes are the same statvfs figure (blocks minus free).
- With `-l`, df skips NFS, SMB and other mounts it classes as remote (including sshfs) before any `statfs`, so a stale mount of that kind cannot block the poll.
- A failed or empty probe does not redraw; header and non-numeric rows are skipped.
- The new tests run under `test/shell`, pass at the head, and fail against the base launcher.

**Optional notes**
- **#13387:** the issue's screenshots compare About's 264.70 GiB (btrfs) with a file scanner's 138.08 GiB for `/`. A freshly started fastfetch reports the same statvfs figure, which on btrfs includes blocks still held by snapshots, so this PR may not resolve that report alone. "Refs #13387", or confirming with the reporter that a closed and reopened About still shows the higher figure, would avoid closing it early.
- **Optional test improvement:** the `df` stub ignores its arguments, so dropping `--output=source,size,used` from the launcher still passes the whole file, although df's default columns would then make every row unreadable and the probe would never fire. A stub that checks its arguments would catch it.
- `df` prints a space in the source column as a space, so a source containing one splits into a non-numeric size and that filesystem is skipped. Reading the two numeric fields from the right of the line avoids this.
</details>

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review and sandboxed shell tests with a stubbed `df` at `8713691`; fastfetch output derived from its source, no live About window.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
